facts.fact: URA's Christine Mirembe says taxpayer accounts will be accessed by biometric fingerprint once the NIN replaces the TIN, and NIRA's Rosemary Kisembo says release of identity data will require biometric authentication and the owner's consent.

UGA.note: Business registration is named only as a source URA could link to; no register described.
Nothing on consumer protection in digital finance.
Nothing on government payments to people.
No count or share of people holding a NIN given.
Nothing on a number at birth.
Nothing on who operates or maintains the ID system.

facts.fact: A government decision makes the NIN the default tax identifier for Ugandan citizens in place of the TIN, and URA says it has started mapping and profiling taxpayers by NIN, with a first phase of NIN submission to end September 2026 and a consent-based second phase.

UGA.note: Nothing stated on the system's state, biometrics or certification beyond NIRA holding the database.

facts.fact: NIRA's Rosemary Kisembo says NIRA will help URA verify that the person registered for tax is the right person against its records, with its database kept separate and data released only on biometric authentication and consent.

UGA.note: No survey figure for account holding.
